en: The tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo found only in Mindoro, is the national animal of the Philippines and is critically endangered.
The sampaguita, known scientifically as Jasminum sambac, is the national flower of the Philippines and symbolizes purity and simplicity.
The Philippine Senate is composed of twenty-four senators who are elected at large by the qualified voters of the entire country.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people built the magnificent Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago using stone and mud walls.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian to study at Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator for rural areas.
The Philippine eagle, also called the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and features a distinctive shaggy crest on its head.
Before the Spanish arrived, early Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using an ancient writing system called Baybayin.
During the Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, Aklan, participants paint their faces with black soot to honor the Santo Niño and indigenous Ati people.
Filipino citizens acquire the right and duty to vote in national elections once they reach the legal voting age of eighteen.
The Supreme Court holds the judicial power of the Philippines and is composed of a Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices.
The narra tree is the national tree of the Philippines, prized for its hard, red wood that resists termites.
